#### The watermark, computed two ways — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** What a watermark is, by computing two of them over the same stream and feeding both to the same trigger.

`heuristic(events)` reads only `events[0..i]`. `perfect(events)` has an inner loop starting at `i + 1` — it reads events that have not arrived, which is precisely why it is unavailable in production and why step 2 is worth staring at.

`closeW0(wm)` takes a watermark array and does not know which generator made it. Same trigger, same window, same events: 15 at index 4 against 19 at index 7. The 34s difference is the price of the correct answer.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-watermark-memory/ch03-watermark-memory.svg" alt="The watermark, computed two ways — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the max is what makes the watermark monotonic</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-watermark-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the max is what makes the watermark monotonic" width="980">

Event id 6 has `et` = 220, which is BELOW `seen` = 260, so the `if` does not fire and `seen` is unchanged. The appended watermark is 200 — the same as the previous one. An out-of-order event cannot move the watermark backwards; it simply does not move it.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — the perfect watermark reads the FUTURE, which is the catch</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-watermark-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: the perfect watermark reads the FUTURE, which is the catch" width="980">

The inner loop starts at `i + 1` — it inspects events that have not arrived. For `i` = 1 it finds id 7's `et` = 50 and so `smallest` is 50. That is the correct answer and the reason it is unavailable: a live pipeline has no `events[j]` for `j > i`.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — so the perfect watermark is stuck at 50 for 6 events</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-watermark-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: so the perfect watermark is stuck at 50 for 6 events" width="980">

For every `i` from 1 to 5 this line finds the same event — id 7, `et` = 50 — so `smallest` is 50 every time. 6 consecutive values, no progress. The heuristic reached 185 over that span, which is 135s of progress it could not justify.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and the window's answer differs by 4</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-watermark-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and the window&#39;s answer differs by 4" width="980">

`closeW0` is given a watermark array and nothing else — it does not know which generator produced it. With the heuristic it returns at `i` = 4 with 15; with the perfect one at `i` = 7 with 19. `priceSeconds` = 34: that is what the correct answer costs, and it required reading the future.

</details>

<sub>The 6-event stall, both published values and the 34s price are computed from the seed and asserted. Generated by `node tools/gen_ch03.js` on `tools/memkit.js`.</sub>
